tasks.task: Build a structured hiring kit for one role

items.when: When the owner decides to fill a role and you need the steps from outcomes to day 90 in order
When one role needs outcomes, a job description, set questions, a work sample and a scorecard
Before an offer, to rule out the hiring mistakes this business has made before
When a panel trusts gut feel, to score each criterion apart and compare with past hires

tasks.task: Write a job description and a fair job ad

items.when: When the usual duties list is dull, to try a version built on the problem the hire must solve
When you need a clear post with only the real requirements and no biased or bloated wording
When a draft or old ad exists and you want it clearer and fairer without changing the job
Before posting, to have a fresh reader go through the ad as a candidate and list what puts them off

tasks.task: Run fair interviews and choose on evidence

items.when: When you want one guided run from interview plan and work test to a fair comparison and replies
When interviewers need set questions with signs of a strong and a weak answer
When you have notes or transcripts and want the comparison tested for bias before the decision
When a finalist's references are due and you need fair questions, a call script and a record sheet
When a candidate needs a clear next-step note or a kind rejection

tasks.task: Draft and check an offer letter

items.when: When a candidate is chosen and you need the letter, the pay package and talking points
Before sending, to flag risky terms and non-compete limits for the place of work

tasks.task: Plan a new hire's first 90 days

items.when: When one person is joining and you need pre-start, day one, week one and 30-60-90 day goals
When the first week needs a half-day schedule with one small real task and who they meet
When the manager wants a guided run with one-on-ones and a look back at day 90
Each week after the start date, to check progress against the plan and what to fix

tasks.task: Write one workplace policy in plain words

items.when: When the team needs one policy as a template with a fixed structure and points for a lawyer
When the policy also needs a manager guide and a rollout plan
When the policy is about home or remote working and the choices are not yet made
When the rules are about shifts, lateness, overtime and absence
When the draft reads like a contract and staff will not get through it
When the policy leans on a law or official guidance, to tie each point to a dated source
When a rule is being added for one bad case and clear expectations might do the job

tasks.task: Draft or update an employee handbook

items.when: When the firm needs handbook sections for its country and size, with a list for a lawyer
When someone asks for a new rule, to find what problem it solves and what it touches
Before a change goes in, to find the other policies it breaks
When an outside rule has changed and you need to know which policies it touches

tasks.task: Announce a policy change with a one-page summary and FAQ

items.when: When a policy is approved and staff need a plain explanation, an announcement and a rollout list
When the news needs manager talking points, a FAQ and an order for who hears first
Before sending, to have a fresh reader go through it as a staff member and list what is unclear
Some weeks after launch, to see whether staff follow the policy and what gets in the way

tasks.task: Review policies and HR practice for gaps

items.when: When one HR area needs a checklist, a file sample, ranked findings and a fix plan
When the owner wants people risks ranked, each with an owner and a response step
Before you send findings, to tie every rule you quote to a dated official source

tasks.task: Draft fair performance reviews from evidence

items.when: When a manager has notes and goals and needs a fair review with pay talk kept apart
When a staff member needs a self-assessment or a manager needs a rating-meeting prep sheet
When reviews run every quarter and each should be drafted from that quarter's goals and notes
When a review is kind but vague and the person will not know what to change

tasks.task: Set up a review cycle with forms, goals and one-on-ones

items.when: When the team needs review forms, goal templates and a guide for a fair rating meeting
When managers need a regular one-on-one with agenda rules, timing and follow-up
When people ask how to move up and the firm has no written levels or growth plans
Every quarter, to check goals, reviews, pay, policies and records are still on track

tasks.task: Prepare a hard conversation with a staff member

items.when: When a manager must raise one behaviour and needs an opening built on facts and one clear ask
When two people are in conflict and you need likely causes, ground rules and what to say
When a formal complaint comes in and you need a plan, an evidence log and a draft memo
When the script dodges the real message or lands as a personal attack

tasks.task: Run a staff pulse survey and act on the results

items.when: When you want a short survey with the follow-up planned before it goes out
When you also need a focus group guide, a way to read results and a manager guide
When results are in, to see which answers you can trust and which questions misled
When feedback is collected and each theme needs an owner, a date and a reply to staff
Each month after, to see which agreed actions are done, overdue or blocked

tasks.task: Build pay bands and a simple pay and benefits plan

items.when: When a handful of roles need pay ranges that are written down and easy to explain
When pay, bonus and benefits all need setting together in one guided run
When the owner needs grades, a bonus formula and a benefits list set against the budget
When current pay must be tested against the market and outliers found

tasks.task: Map HR records and set retention and access rules

items.when: When staff records sit across email, drives and apps and nobody knows what to delete when
Before a new tool or a role change, to check who can see which staff data

tasks.task: Plan a calm exit and handover for someone leaving

items.when: When someone has resigned or a contract is ending and nothing must be missed
When you need exit interview questions and a handover plan tied to the leave date
When the leaver must write a note the next person can run from on day one
When the firm is ending the job and needs a fair exit plan, risk flags and the team message
When the owner keeps putting off a hard exit and the team already knows

tasks.task: Plan absence cover and cut key-person risk

items.when: When one person is going on leave and you need a cover map and task-by-task notes
When one role has no backup and each critical task needs a trained second person
When too much work lives in the founder's head and deputies need handover notes

tasks.task: Set up for a first employee or a hire in another country

items.when: When a founder is making a first hire and needs dated set-up tasks and accountant questions
When the hire lives abroad and you must weigh your own entity against an employer of record
When it is unclear if the person is a contractor or an employee and the risk needs a first check
Before the checklist goes out, to tie each legal step to a dated official source

tasks.task: Write a role guide or handover pack for one job

items.when: When a job's routine work needs writing down with who does what and the edge cases
When the pack must cover open work, contacts and what to do first

tasks.task: Set up a people-ops starter kit and people report

items.when: When you need to see the staff journey from first week to exit, with pain points and fixes
When gaps in contracts, records or cover need ranking with owners
When the owner wants a few people measures defined and a monthly report they will read
When you have a staff spreadsheet and need headcount and turnover trends for leaders
Every three months, to run the whole kit against what changed

tasks.task: Answer staff questions from the company's own rules

items.when: When someone asks about leave, travel or expenses and the answer must match the handbook
Before you reply, to check each line of the answer points to a rule the firm really has

tasks.task: Plan wellbeing support, adjustments and return to work

items.when: When the team needs a wellbeing plan, a manager guide and return-to-work steps
When someone asks for an adjustment and the manager needs a guide, options and a review plan
When absence rules are unwritten and people are treated differently

tasks.task: Plan an internship with real work and fair selection

items.when: When a first-time host needs a supervised learning plan and review questions for the supervisor
When interns must be chosen on a short task and a scorecard, not on who they know
When the intern post should ask only for what a student could really have
When the supervisor needs a weekly check-in format with follow-up

tasks.task: Find candidates and screen applications fairly

items.when: When no one is applying and you need a fit profile, a search plan and first messages
When resumes come in batches and each must be scored the same way against the guide

always.when: At the start of any sizeable job, to capture the real business, its rules and its country first
Before anything goes to staff, to cut legal and HR wording down to plain words
Whenever the work states what the law requires, to give each point a dated source or cut it

helpers.when: When the job needs sourcing, outreach and a managed candidate pipeline, not just the hiring kit
When pay bands need market data, payroll set-up or a pay equity check
When a change affects the whole company and needs a full message plan
When survey results need deeper reading and a programme of actions
When onboarding or a policy needs real training built, not just a checklist
When a policy area is regulated and needs a control check beyond HR practice

gaps: No library item writes a reference letter for a former employee or other formal HR letters such as a written warning or probation outcome
No library item builds a performance improvement plan or a probation review
No library item checks several performance reviews against each other for consistent ratings and wording
No library item writes a remote team working agreement; the only team agreement item is for student projects
Internship work is thin: one learning-plan workflow, nothing for school outreach emails, a supervisor guide or an end-of-internship review
No library item builds an HR records map or retention schedule beyond the kit prompt
No library item checks right-to-work or visa steps for a hire
No library item makes two or three clearly different versions of a staff announcement or job ad to choose between
No library item writes a role guide for one job; the procedure writer covers tasks, not the whole role
No library item tracks mandatory training or builds a training record
The library has no tool guide for an HR system, a survey tool or an applicant tracker
